narrationTexts: I'll look at the report command first so the plan is grounded in the actual code.
finalText:
Here's the shape of it. Three files, ~63 lines total, and the pipeline is already split the way you'd want: `buildRows()` (src/report.js:11) produces the data, `toTable()` (src/format.js:14) renders it, `main()` (src/cli.js:8) wires them.

## Plan

1. **`src/format.js`** — add `toJson(rows)` next to `toTable`, exported alongside it. Just `JSON.stringify(rows, null, 2)`. It goes here because this file is "how rows get printed"; `report.js` stays render-agnostic.
2. **`src/cli.js`** — parse `--json` out of the args after the `report` check, pick the renderer, keep the single `process.stdout.write(... + '\n')`. Update `USAGE` to `usage: cli.js report [--json]`.
3. **Unknown flags** — currently anything after `report` is silently ignored. I'd reject unrecognized args with the usage error, so `--jsno` fails loudly instead of printing a table. Say the word if you'd rather keep it permissive.

No changes to `src/report.js`.

## One judgment call worth your input

"Same data" is ambiguous here, because the two stages don't carry the same fields. `buildRows()` emits six fields per row — `id, suite, status, ms, owner, slow` — but `COLUMNS` (src/format.js:7) prints only four; `owner` and `slow` are dropped, and the comment there says that's a width concession, with "anything that needs the whole row has to go back to buildRows(), not to this."

So I'd emit **all six fields** in JSON: the drop is a terminal-formatting limitation, not part of the data, and a machine-readable output has no width problem. That also makes `--json` actually useful — `owner` is the field you'd group by, and `slow` is the derived one you'd filter on.

The alternative reading is "JSON of exactly the table you see," i.e. four fields. I don't recommend it — it would bake a display constraint into the machine format — but it's a real reading of "same data," and it's cheap to switch. Sort order (slowest first) is preserved either way.

Tell me which, and whether to be strict on unknown flags, and I'll make the change.
